members.name: stream-models
members.para: Three ways to read the rows as they arrive; pick by what the connection and your loop need:

listheader.description: Buffer; threads; connection held until; stall protection

item.description: None: no row is read ahead; your own thread, with no producer task and no channel; until you pull the last row; yes, on every pull.

Up to bufferSize rows (default 1,024; it counts rows, not bytes); a producer task and your loop; until the read ends, or, once the buffer is full, until the stall timeout passes without a pull (never with an infinite timeout); yes, once the buffer is full.
Unbounded: pooled chunks, the whole result if you are slow; a producer task and your loop; until the read ends, however slowly you read; none.

members.para: Which to use: a fast loop, Stream; slow or async work per row, StreamBuffered; to free the connection as soon as possible, ToPooledStream.

All three are lazy: calling one does nothing until the first MoveNextAsync. A slow or hung database read is bounded by the command's CommandTimeout and your cancellation token on every one of them; the stall timeout is only about a slow consumer. A cancel or a dispose stops the read promptly only as far as the provider honors the cancellation.
